fichas.title: Symbols and Colours Used on Plans and Sections
fichas.summary: Reference table pairing monochrome drawing patterns and colours with materials or elements, including masonry, earth, concrete, metal, timber, insulation, sealants, and existing building elements.
uses: Identify materials and building elements in plans and sections

fichas.title: Construction Drawing Symbols
fichas.summary: Explains abbreviations and conventions for openings, grooves, ducts, and breakthroughs in slabs, floors, foundations, and walls. The examples show descriptions, labels, dimension notation, and plan or elevation depictions. Dimension notation uses width, depth, and height; location and reference levels include under, over, top, bottom, unfinished floor, and finished floor.
uses: Represent and label construction openings, grooves, ducts, and breakthroughs on drawings

fichas.title: Symbols for Building Permit Applications
fichas.summary: Illustrates plan symbols for existing and planned roads and buildings, public green space, parks, allotments, camping and weekend sites, sports fields, swimming pools, children's playgrounds, cemeteries, and special facilities.
uses: Depict site conditions and planned uses on building permit application drawings

fichas.title: Symbols Used in Open Spaces Planning
fichas.summary: Shows conventions for natural monuments and protected areas, tree protection and removal, partly removed bush groups, and boundaries of soil-contamination areas. Tree symbols are annotated with species, trunk centre, crown radius, and trunk diameter; existing and planned vegetation use different line styles.
uses: Represent protected natural features, vegetation status, and contaminated-soil boundaries in open-space plans
